# What is the biggest stadium in the world? The ranking by capacity
From North Korea to the United States, these are the largest stadiums in the world

24/06/2020

![](https://www.webuildvalue.com/wp-content/themes/webuildvalue_cambe/app/_src/images/share.svg)

**Once upon a time there were amphitheatres, used for gladiatorial games and celebrations.** Wrestlers were joined by ferocious animals like lions, tigers, bears and even rhinos. The largest amphitheatre in the world, as is known, was and still is the Colosseum, capable of containing about 75,000 people.

**Today the amphitheatres have been replaced by stadiums**, where football players clash instead of gladiators. However, there are not many stadiums that manage to exceed the ancient capacity of the Colosseum.

## What about the biggest stadium in Europe?
#### Rungrado May Day Stadium
**Rungrado May Day Stadium** – **The biggest stadium in the world** is where you do not expect it – **North Korea**, in Pyongyang. Firmly at the top of the table with its **150,000 seats**, it was **inaugurated in 1989.** More than football – although hosting some North Korean national games – the stadium is dedicated to **mass performances organised by the regime.** In recent years, **the largest stadium in the world** has undergone restoration work, with a significant reduction in seating capacity.

#### Salt Lake Stadium
**Salt Lake Stadium**– Even the second largest stadium in the world is in Asia, more specifically in **Calcutta**. With **120,000 seats,** Salt Lake Stadium is the home of the Mohun Bagan A.C., East Bengal Football Club and Mohammedan S.C. On special occasions – and in a way that is not entirely regular – it is said that the structure has come to accommodate 131,000 people. It **was built in 1984, has an elliptical shape and is organised on three rings.**

#### Michigan Stadium
**Michigan Stadium**– We move to the United States, to Ann Arbor. Built in **1927** and expanded on several occasions, the structure nicknamed **“The Big House” accommodates** up to **115,000 people.** This capacity was also achieved thanks to building the first tiers below ground level, thus compensating for the reduced height of the structure.

#### Azteca Stadium
**Azteca Stadium** – The fifth largest stadium in the world is located in **Mexico**, and is the home of Club América. Built between 1963 and 1966, it is the only stadium in the world to have hosted two finals of the world football championship, in 1970 and 1986. **The seats are a total of 105,000, structured on three rings.** Two curiosities: **here is where was played what is remembered as the “Game of the Century” between Italy and West Germany in 1970.** It ended 4-3 for the Azzurri. Then **there was the 1986 “Goal of the Century” by Diego Armando Maradona.**

#### Ohio Stadium
**[Ohio Stadium](https://www.webuildvalue.com/en/reportage/ohio-stadium.html)** – This stadium has **104,900 seats.** **Inaugurated in Columbus in 1922**, it mainly hosts football matches. Up until 2014, it was used only during the day for lack of lighting. The Ohio Stadium was also the stage of numerous concerts: from Pink Floyd to Genesis to the Rolling Stones to Metallica.

#### Kyle Field
**Kyle Field** – The seventh largest stadium in the world is in **Texas** and is the home of the Aggies, a team from the Football Bowl Subdivision of the National Collegiate Athletics Association. Built in 1927 and expanded several times, it has a total of 102,700 seats.

#### Neyland Stadium
**Neyland Stadium** – This Tennessee-based facility in Knoxville also **[ranks among the world’s largest stadiums](https://www.webuildvalue.com/en/reportage/the-top-10-large-stadiums-in-the-usa.html) in terms of capacity.** Dedicated above all to college football matches, the stadium boasts **102,455 seats.** Until 2010 the capacity was significantly higher, but it was reduced to ensure greater security.

#### Tiger Stadium
**Tiger Stadium** – The penultimate stage of our ranking is in Louisiana and has **102,321 seats.** **Nicknamed “Death Valley”** to frighten opposing football teams, **the Tiger Stadium was inaugurated in 1924.**

#### Bryant-Denny Stadium
**Bryant-Denny Stadium** – The 10th largest stadium in the world is in **Alabama** with an official capacity of 101,821 seats. It was inaugurated in 1929.

This ranking of the biggest stadiums in the world, in the coming years, is destined to undergo changes. **To undermine the positions of the podium there will in fact be “The Lion of Babylon” stadium, a structure of about 135,000 seats** and a futuristic design that will be built in Iraq.

**The genesis of this work** is curious: on the occasion of a friendly between the national football teams of Saudi Arabia and Iraq, the Saudi King Salam bet with the Iraqi Prime Minister Al-Abadi that, in case of a defeat for his team, he would build a gigantic stadium. Against all odds, Iraq managed to defeat Saudi Arabia, already qualified for the world championships and widely favoured, thus giving way, **by bet**, to the design of this pharaonic stadium.

One might think that, since football is the most popular sport in many European countries, many of **the biggest stadiums in the world** would be found there. Not so: in fact, in **the top** 10, there are no Italian structures nor European ones to be mentioned. **[The largest European stadium](https://www.webuildvalue.com/en/reportage/biggest-european-football-stadiums.html), the [Camp Nou](https://www.webuildvalue.com/en/reportage/new-camp-nou.html)**, the legendary arena of **Barcelona**, hosts just under **100,000 seats**, a number far from those of the biggest stadiums in the world. Despite being able to count on numerous services such as a museum, **the “blaugrana” camp stops at 14th place in the world rankings.** If compared with **the biggest stadiums in the world**, even **the Italian giants** find themselves smaller: with **the Meazza in Milan**, also known as San Siro, that does not exceed **80,000 seats** and **the Olympic stadium in Rome** at **70,000.**

## Size isn’t everything. But it sure is something.
So here’s our 2026 ranking of the largest stadiums in the world by capacity: not just the numbers, but the stories behind them.

**The 18 largest stadiums in the world by capacity (2026 ranking):**

1. **Narendra Modi Stadium**: 132,000 (Ahmedabad, India)
2. **Rungrado May Day Stadium**: 113,281 (Pyongyang, North Korea)
3. **Camp Nou**: 105,000 post-expansion / 99,354 current (Barcelona, Spain). Europe’s largest after the 2026 Espai Barça expansion.
4. **Michigan Stadium**: 107,601 (Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA)
5. **Beaver Stadium**: 106,572 (University Park, Pennsylvania, USA)
6. **Ohio Stadium**: 102,780 (Columbus, Ohio, USA)
7. **Kyle Field**: 102,733 (College Station, Texas, USA)
8. **Tiger Stadium**: 102,321 (Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA)
9. **Neyland Stadium**: 101,915 (Knoxville, Tennessee, USA)
10. **Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium**: 100,119 (Austin, Texas, USA)
11. **Bryant-Denny Stadium**: 100,077 (Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA)
12. **Melbourne Cricket Ground**: 100,024 (Melbourne, Australia)
13. **Wembley Stadium**: 90,000 (London, England)
14. **Estadio Azteca**: 87,523 (Mexico City, Mexico). Latin America’s largest, hosting the 2026 World Cup opener.
15. **MetLife Stadium**: 82,500 (East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA). Hosting the 2026 World Cup Final.
16. **Stade de France**: 80,698 (Saint-Denis, France)
17. **AT&T Stadium**: 80,000 (Arlington, Texas, USA). Expandable to over 100,000 for major events.
18. **SoFi Stadium**: 70,240 (Inglewood, California, USA)

## 1. Narendra Modi Stadium — 132,000 (Ahmedabad, India)
The world’s actual largest stadium isn’t a football venue. It’s a cricket ground.

Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad holds 132,000 spectators, which makes it not only the world’s largest cricket stadium but the world’s largest stadium of any kind. It opened in its current rebuilt form in 2020, replacing the older Sardar Patel Stadium that occupied the same site since 1982. The complete rebuild was driven by the Gujarat Cricket Association at a cost of around $114 million, and the result is a venue that genuinely changes how you think about what “big” means for a sports facility.

The architecture is striking. A modern oval bowl with two tiers all the way around, an LED-illuminated exterior, four dressing rooms that can host two simultaneous matches, and a 55-meter-wide playing field. When it’s full for an India vs Pakistan cricket match, the noise level is documented to rival anything in football.

Most Western readers underestimate this stadium because cricket coverage in North America and Europe is limited, and the stadium’s name change in 2021 (to honor India’s prime minister) generated political coverage that overshadowed the sporting story. But by capacity, Narendra Modi Stadium sits comfortably above every other stadium on Earth, about 19,000 seats clear of the next-largest venue.

**132,000 seats** — Narendra Modi Stadium is the largest sports venue in the world by capacity, roughly 19,000 seats above Rungrado May Day Stadium at #2.

## 2. Rungrado May Day Stadium — 113,281 (Pyongyang, North Korea)
The biggest stadium in the football world is one almost nobody reading this will ever visit.

Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang has held the top football-capacity spot since it opened in 1989. Its official capacity is 113,281, though some sources have questioned whether that number reflects reality. The stadium was originally built for the 13th World Festival of Youth and Students, and its scalloped roof design (16 arches meant to resemble a magnolia blossom) is genuinely striking.

Here’s what makes it strange, though. Rungrado isn’t really used as a sports venue anymore. It hosts the Mass Games, North Korea’s massive choreographed propaganda spectacle, and the occasional political rally. Satellite imagery suggests it’s gone through periods of disrepair. Football matches have been played there, but irregularly.

So yes, it’s technically the second-largest stadium in the world and the largest football venue. But it’s also arguably the least accessible and least active stadium on this entire list. Make of that what you will.

**113,281 seats** — Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang has held the world’s largest football-stadium spot since 1989, though its actual regular attendance remains a mystery.

## 3. Camp Nou — 105,000 post-expansion (Barcelona, Spain)
Here’s where it gets interesting for 2026.

[Camp Nou](https://meetstadium.com/stadiums/camp-nou/) has historically held around 99,354 seats, making it the largest stadium in Europe. The [Espai Barça renovation](https://meetstadium.com/journal/camp-nou-espai-barca-renovation-2026/) (a massive, years-in-the-making project that’s cost north of 1.5 billion euros) is pushing that number to approximately 105,000 upon full completion, targeted for 2026.

As of mid-2026, the venue is operating with reduced temporary capacity (~60,000-80,000 depending on phase) while construction continues around live matches.

When it’s done, Camp Nou won’t just be Europe’s largest stadium. It’ll be one of the most modern. But from a pure “wow factor” standpoint, the new Camp Nou is going to be something.

We position Camp Nou at #3 in this ranking based on its post-expansion 105,000 capacity. By current capacity (99,354), it sits at #12, below the row of US college football venues that fill the middle of this list.

**99,354 to 105,000** — Camp Nou’s Espai Barca renovation adds over 5,600 seats, a full roof, and a price tag north of 1.5 billion euros, making it the largest and most expensive stadium overhaul in European football history.

## 14. Estadio Azteca — 87,523 (Mexico City, Mexico)
[Estadio Azteca](https://meetstadium.com/stadiums/estadio-azteca/) is the only stadium in the world that’s hosted two FIFA World Cup finals (1970 and 1986). At 87,523, it’s not the biggest anymore, but its history is unmatched.

This is where Maradona scored the “Hand of God” goal and the “Goal of the Century” in the same match. This is where Pele lifted the World Cup for the third time. The altitude (2,200 meters above sea level) makes it one of the most physically demanding places to play on Earth.

And here’s the big news: Azteca is set to host matches during the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://meetstadium.com/world-cup-2026/), including the opening match. It’ll become the first stadium to feature in three World Cups. That’s a record that may never be broken.

For more on Azteca’s unique three-World-Cup record, see our journal piece [Estadio Azteca: The Only Stadium to Host Three World Cup Openers](https://meetstadium.com/journal/estadio-azteca-three-world-cup-openers/).

## Honorable mentions
- [Maracana](https://meetstadium.com/stadiums/maracana/) in Rio de Janeiro once held nearly 200,000 people. The 1950 World Cup final’s official paid attendance was 173,850, with FIFA’s total attendance figure of 199,854 including non-paying entries. That’s the most-attended football match in history by either measure. Today it’s down to about 78,838 after multiple renovations. Still one of the most famous stadiums on the planet.
- **Bukit Jalil National Stadium** in Kuala Lumpur holds 87,411 and is one of the largest stadiums in Asia, though it rarely fills to capacity.
- **FNB Stadium** (Soccer City) in Johannesburg holds 94,736 and hosted the 2010 World Cup final. It’s the largest stadium in Africa, and its calabash-inspired design is genuinely beautiful.
- **Misr Stadium** in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital holds 93,940 and is one of the largest stadiums in Africa, completed as part of Egypt’s effort to bid for major continental tournaments.

## Frequently Asked Questions
What is the largest stadium in the world in 2026? Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, India, is the largest stadium in the world by capacity at 132,000 seats. It is a cricket ground, not a football venue, and sits roughly 19,000 seats clear of the next-largest, Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang at 113,281.

What is the largest stadium in the United States? Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, nicknamed 'The Big House,' is the largest stadium in the United States and the largest in the Americas at 107,601 capacity.

Eleven stadiums have a permanent capacity above 100,000 in 2026, and Camp Nou becomes the twelfth at 105,000 once its Espai Barça expansion is complete. Most of the 100,000-plus venues are US college football stadiums, including Michigan (107,601), Beaver (106,572), Ohio (102,780), Kyle Field (102,733), Tiger (102,321), and Neyland (101,915).

What is the largest football stadium in the world? Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, is the largest stadium that hosts football, at 113,281 capacity. Among club football grounds, Camp Nou in Barcelona becomes Europe's largest at approximately 105,000 once its Espai Barça expansion is finished, up from its previous 99,354.

Why is Camp Nou ranked above Michigan Stadium even though Michigan is bigger? We rank Camp Nou at number three on its post-expansion target of 105,000, reflecting its status as Europe's largest stadium after the Espai Barça project. By strict 2026 capacity, Michigan Stadium (107,601) is larger, and Camp Nou's current configuration is 99,354 mid-expansion.

What is the largest stadium hosting the 2026 World Cup? AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, is the largest 2026 World Cup venue at roughly 94,000 for the tournament, using its end-zone standing-room sections. Estadio Azteca in Mexico City follows at 87,523, and MetLife Stadium, which hosts the final, runs 78,576 for the World Cup. No 2026 host venue reaches the 100,000-plus mark.

# What is the biggest stadium in the world? See which have the highest capacity.
[![Portrait of Clare Mulroy](https://www.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/authoring-images/2024/06/03/USAT/73954566007-clare-mulroy-headshots-02.jpg?crop=2972,2973,x0,y421&width=48&height=48&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Clare Mulroy](https://www.usatoday.com/staff/7713150001/clare-mulroy/)

USA TODAY

July 28, 2024Updated Nov. 19, 2024, 5:39 p.m. ET

[Share to Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?display=popup&app_id=1279862243338849&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2F2024%2F07%2F28%2Fbiggest-largest-stadiums-in-world%2F74462698007%2F)[Share to Twitter](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2F2024%2F07%2F28%2Fbiggest-largest-stadiums-in-world%2F74462698007%2F&text=What%20is%20the%20biggest%20stadium%20in%20the%20world%3F%20See%20which%20have%20the%20highest%20capacity.&via=usatoday)[Share by email](mailto:?subject=What%20is%20the%20biggest%20stadium%20in%20the%20world%3F%20See%20which%20have%20the%20highest%20capacity.%20-%20from%20USA%20TODAY&body=What%20is%20the%20biggest%20stadium%20in%20the%20world%3F%20See%20which%20have%20the%20highest%20capacity.%0A%0AThe%20biggest%20stadium%20in%20the%20world%20may%20not%20be%20in%20the%20U.S.%2C%20but%20eight%20of%20the%20top%2010%20largest%20are.%20Here%27s%20which%20college%20football%20venues%20make%20the%20cut.%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20usatoday.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2F2024%2F07%2F28%2Fbiggest-largest-stadiums-in-world%2F74462698007%2F)

Every two years, we [watch Olympic athletes compete](https://www.usatoday.com/sports/olympics/) at some of the world’s largest sporting venues. This year, more than [10,000 athletes](https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024) competed in the 35 [venues designated](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2024/07/15/paris-olympics-venues-guide/74004292007/) for the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, including the Stade de France, the country’s largest stadium.

Created for the 1998 Football World Cup, the Stade de France has hosted World Athletics Championships, Rugby World Cups and a Euro Football Championship. It can seat [more than 80,000 fans](https://parisjetaime.com/eng/culture/stade-de-france-p3568), according to the Paris Tourist Office.

But while the Stade de France’s seating capacity may sound gargantuan, it doesn’t even crack the top 10 list.

## What is the biggest stadium?
Located in Pyongyang, North Korea, the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium is the largest stadium in the world. It has 150,000 seats and a [total floor area](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Rungrado-1st-of-May-Stadium) of over 2.2 million square feet. It stands eight stories high.

Rungrado 1st of May Stadium – also known as the May Day stadium – was built with its overpowering size in mind. North Korea constructed the stadium in 1989 during the Cold War, just a year after South Korea hosted the Summer Olympics. Tensions between the North and the South caused the two nations to look for any opportunity to one-up each other. This resulted in North Korea creating [an Olympics-style competition of its own](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/02/04/world/asia/north-korea-olympics.html), expanding a major airport and constructing new streets, a skyscraper and the May Day stadium, which cost $200 million to build, The New York Times reported.

However, it’s not the only stadium that can fit over 100,000 people. Here are the top 10 largest stadiums in the world [and their capacities](https://olympics.com/en/news/largest-stadium-world-venue-capacity-spectator-seats), according to the International Olympic Committee and official seating records:

1. Rungrado 1st of May Stadium (Pyongyang, North Korea): 150,000
2. Narendra Modi Stadium (Ahmedabad, India): 132,000
3. Michigan Stadium (Michigan, U.S.): 107,601
4. Beaver Stadium (Pennsylvania, U.S.): 106,572
5. Ohio Stadium (Ohio, U.S.): 102,780
6. Kyle Field (Texas, U.S.): 102,733
7. Tiger Stadium (Louisiana, U.S.): 102,321
8. Neyland Stadium (Tennessee, U.S.): 101,915
9. Bryant-Denny Stadium (Alabama, U.S.): 101,821
10. Darrel K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium (Texas, U.S.): 100,119

## What is the largest stadium in the U.S.?
The largest stadium in the U.S. is Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Michigan. It’s dubbed “The Big House” for a reason – the University of Michigan sports arena has a [seating capacity of 107,601](https://diversity.umich.edu/2015/08/seating-capacity-at-michigan-stadium-slightly-reduced/), making it the largest stadium in college football, in the U.S. and even in the entire western hemisphere. It was [ranked No. 3 this year](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2024/07/18/michigan-stadium-college-football-stadium-rankings-espn-big-house/74456652007/) in an ESPN ranking of the [best stadiums in college football,](https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/40559641/top-25-college-football-stadiums-lsu-rose-bowl-michigan) coming in behind LSU’s Tiger Stadium and UCLA’s Rose Bowl.

![Aptly named "The Big House," Michigan Stadium is the largest stadium in the U.S. and the second-largest in the world.](https://www.usatoday.com/gcdn/-mm-/43357c0c3c2f4747b98aa9fba150b940a7335403/c=0-106-2048-1262/local/-/media/USATODAY/USATODAY/2014/09/18/1411034688000-Ann-Arbor.jpg?width=660&height=373&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

Here are the top [10 largest college football stadiums](https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2018-07-30/25-biggest-college-football-stadiums-country) in the U.S., according to the NCAA:

1. Michigan Stadium (Ann Arbor, Michigan): 107,601
2. Beaver Stadium (University Park, Pennsylvania): 106,572
3. Ohio Stadium (Columbus, Ohio): 102,780
4. Kyle Field (College Station, Texas): 102,733
5. Tiger Stadium (Baton Rouge, Louisiana): 102,321
6. Neyland Stadium (Knoxville, Tennessee): 101,915
7. Bryant-Denny Stadium (Tuscaloosa, Alabama): 101,821
8. Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium (Austin, Texas): 100,119
9. Sanford Stadium (Athens, Georgia): 92,746
10. Rose Bowl (Pasadena, California): 91,136

Though not technically stadiums, there are many U.S. motor speedways with seating capacities that rival the largest stadiums in the country. For example, the Bristol Motor Speedway in Tennessee, which has a [“stadium-like structure,”](https://www.bristolmotorspeedway.com/media/) has a [spectator capacity of 162,000,](https://nascar101.nascar.com/nascar-tracks-bristol-motor-speedway/) according to NASCAR. The Texas Motor Speedway has a seating capacity of about 150,000 but has [seen crowds of over 200,000,](https://www.texasmonthly.com/arts-entertainment/has-texas-motor-speedway-been-lapped/) Texas Monthly reports.

## Just Curious for more? We've got you covered.
USA TODAY is exploring the questions you and others ask every day. From ["When did the Olympics start?"](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2024/05/11/when-did-the-olympics-start/73498623007/) to ["What is my state nickname?"](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2023/01/29/official-state-nicknames-50-united-states/11032943002/) to ["Which country has the most Olympic medals?"](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2023/05/10/which-country-has-most-olympic-medals/11414925002/) – we're striving to find answers to the most common questions you ask every day. Head to our [Just Curious section](https://www.usatoday.com/just-curious/) to see what else we can answer for you.

# **The 9 Biggest Stadiums In The World**
## Which stadium has the biggest capacity? Read on to find out…
![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58ee0b551e5b6c8ff18b94ad/9ba18df2-0185-4cdf-9441-bfe117dd1fc4/79542ff06ea9211d28e3dc4e4739e2ac+%281%29.jpg)

The iconic Camp Nou football stadium, Barcelona

[There are hundreds of stadiums](https://thesporting.blog/blog/sporting-trivia-how-many-stadiums-are-there-in-the-world) in the world. They contribute to local sports and tourism economies, creating jobs and generating revenue from ticket and merchandise sales.

A beautiful stadium also showcases a city's infrastructure, history, tradition and culture to a global audience.

In this article, read about the 9 largest stadiums in the world by capacity.

All of these stadiums include state-of-the-art facilities, large seating capacities, [cutting-edge technology](https://thesporting.blog/blog/the-use-of-technology-in-football-var) features, innovative designs and beautiful locations that promote enthusiasm for fans.

## **1. Rungrado 1st of May Stadium: 150,000 Capacity**
North Korea's national stadium is the largest facility in the world.

The North Korean government built the stadium in response to South Korea's Olympic stadium. [The construction](http://stadiumdb.com/stadiums/pkr/rungrado_may_day_stadium) of the national stadium took two years and five months.

In addition, the stadium can accommodate up to 150,000 spectators, allowing them to watch football matches or enjoy entertainment and cultural events.

[The unique roof design](https://olympics.com/en/news/biggest-football-stadium-world-capacity) is the most prominent feature of North Korea's national stadium. It has 16 petal-shaped segments supported by 11,000 outer steel sheets.

North Korea's National Stadium is a prime venue for football events, hosting high-profile matches, including both international and national.

## **3. Camp Nou: 98,000 Capacity**
Camp Nou is the third largest stadium in the world, hosting football matches and events.

Camp Nou is a [prominent Spanish football stadium](https://thesporting.blog/blog/spanish-football-stadiums), and it can accommodate more than 98,000 spectators.

This stadium is home to [FC Barcelona](https://thesporting.blog/blog/the-5-greatest-players-in-fc-barcelona-history), one of Europe's most prominent and beloved football clubs.

This stadium’s unique design is awe-inspiring, providing fans with spectacular pitch views thanks to the steep seating arrangement.
